claim: The new @role: resolution check (and the references/*.md check) run err() inside a `grep | sort | sed | while read` pipeline subshell; FAIL=1 set there never reaches the parent shell, so detected drift exits 0 and prints 'CLEAN — no drift.' plus an unconditional 'ok: role files present, registered, @role refs resolve' line.
evidence: Controlled repro (tmp copy of script, prompts/x.md containing '@role:ghostrole', all other checks passing): output 'DRIFT: @role:ghostrole referenced but agents/ghostrole.md missing' + 'CLEAN — no drift.' + EXIT CODE 0. `FAIL=0; err(){ FAIL=1; }; echo x | while read r; do err $r; done; echo $FAIL` → 0.
runtimeTrigger: Any prompt/skill/agent file referencing @role:<name> without a matching agents/<name>.md or registry row (or a dangling references/*.md): check-drift.sh (pre-commit hook + CI) passes silently.
crossReferences: CHANGELOG.md (claims 'Red-tested' — red test must have asserted stdout, not exit code)

claim: roleBody's first regex only strips a LEADING HTML comment, but every real role file (agents/worker.md, reviewer.md, scout.md, quality-reviewer.md) places the dispatch-note HTML comment AFTER the '# Role:' line, so the orchestrator-facing dispatch note is injected verbatim into every resolved subagent prompt.
evidence: Live run: roleBody(fs.readFileSync('agents/worker.md','utf8')) returns a body starting with "<!-- Verbatim subagent system prompt — pasted into `prompt:` by the orchestrator.\n Dispatch policy..." — the inline comment says 'Drop leading HTML comment (the dispatch note)' and it is not dropped.
runtimeTrigger: Any subagent dispatch using prompt:'@role:worker'|'@role:reviewer'|'@role:scout'|'@role:quality-reviewer' — the meta-instructions meant for the orchestrator reach the subagent system prompt every time.
crossReferences: tests/extension.test.ts (WORKER fixture has the same order but only asserts '# Role:' removal — gap in test)

claim: missingFinalVerdicts compares done-task count against the NUMBER OF REVIEW FILES containing '**ok: true**', not per-task verdicts — ok:true files from a previous, non-archived (abandoned) plan, or a single file legitimately covering multiple tasks, mask real missing verdicts (Math.max clamps to 0).
evidence: finalOkTrue = reviewFiles.filter((f) => /\*\*ok: true\*\*/.test(f.content)).length; missingFinalVerdicts = max(0, doneTasks - finalOkTrue). Reviews are only archived on SHIP (prompts/review.md:122-130); an abandoned plan leaves its ok:true files in .workflows/reviews for the next plan's watchdog to count.
runtimeTrigger: New plan with done tasks while stale ok:true review files from an abandoned prior plan remain in .workflows/reviews → drift reminder suppressed.
crossReferences: agents/execution-doctrine.md verdict artifact format (one file per task-id, rounds appended)

claim: changelogPending is derived purely from plan statuses (done === total) and never inspects CHANGELOG.md, so after /review Stage 3 writes the entry the 'plan complete — SHIP requires a CHANGELOG.md entry' line can re-fire as a false positive whenever any other drift boolean flips (state-key change re-notifies with the stale changelog part). Additionally the file header comment (and CHANGELOG) promise 'Reminds once per new gap count (no spam)' while the implementation dedupes on the boolean state ('one reminder per episode') — count changes never re-notify.
evidence: computeDocsDrift: changelogPending = total > 0 && done === total — no CHANGELOG.md read anywhere in the watchdog; header comment extensions/index.ts:11-12 'Reminds once per new gap count' vs inline comment 'one reminder per episode, not per count change' vs dedupe key built from booleans only.
runtimeTrigger: Plan complete + CHANGELOG already written → any hygiene/docs boolean flip re-injects the changelog reminder; gap count 1→3 with booleans unchanged → no reminder despite the header's promise.
crossReferences: README.md 'one reminder per drift episode' (third wording)
